newsitem.title: CHILE: Sherwin Williams buys Chilean paint maker.
newsitem.headline: Sherwin Williams buys Chilean paint maker.

text.p: Paint maker Sherwin-Williams Co. has bought Chilean paint company Pinturas Andina SA in the Cleveland-based firm's second major acquisition in Chile in the past year, an official at Andina said.

Sherwin-Williams bought Andina for an undisclosed sum Friday and plans to wrap it into the U.S. company's local affiliate, Sherwin-Williams Chile SA, said the official at Andina, who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Sherwin-Williams confirmed it purchased Andina through its wholly owned Sherwin-Williams Chile SA subsidiary. It said Andina, which has sales of between $10 million and $20 million, produces and sells architectural coatings through independent dealers and 16 company-owned stores.
Andina, which has served the Chilean market for more than 60 years, has been a licensee of Sherwin-Williams since 1968, Sherwin-Williams said.

The purchase has added to a gradual strengthening of the U.S. company's position in the Chilean paint market, putting it only behind Industrias Tricolor SA, owned by Chile's Larrain company, in terms of sales.

Andina is Chile's fourth largest maker of paints and related construction materials. The Andina official said the Chilean company had profits last year of about $1 million on sales of between $15 million and $20 million.

Sherwin-Williams last year bought Andina's competitor, Industria de Pintura Stierling and a related company, Pinturas Baco. With the new purchase, Sherwin-Williams' sales in Chile should exceed $50 million a year, said the official.

"This acquisition (of Andina) in conjunction with our previous acquisition of Baco Stierling gives us a broad coatings business base in Chile with strong reputations and well-known brand names," Sherwin-Williams Chairman John Breen said in a statement. "These acquisitions provide us with a significant participation in the growth of Chile and further strengthens our position in the Mercosur market."
Details on how Andina, which has a factory and about 16 sales outlets, will be incorporated into Sherwin-Williams Chile are still being worked out, the official said.
Sherwin-Williams has been gradually increasing its reach in Latin America, with subsidiaries in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina.
